newsitem.title: UK: WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUGUST 14.
newsitem.headline: WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUGUST 14.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

NEW YORK - Advertising spending on the Internet and online services will grow to an estimated $7.7 billion in 2002 from $301 million last year, as more people go online and advertising models become more refined, says a report by research group Jupiter Communications.

FRANKFURT - Interactive advertising could be available to viewers of DF1 by the end of the month, says the digital television channel. The new technology will allow viewers to switch between various ads for a single product with the press of a button on a digital decoder box.

LONDON - Saatchi & Saatchi Advertising says it has won a seven million pound ($11.1 million) UK account for Typhoo tea and London Herb & Spice Company, which belong to Premier Beverages. Saatchi & Saatchi took the business away from incumbent Delaney Fletcher Bozell.
PARIS - Publicis, the French advertising agency, has borrowed lines straight from the Bible for its campaign to promote the visit to France next week by Pope John Paul II.
LONDON - Advertising agency DDB Brisbane in Australia says it has retained the Golden Casket Corporation's Gold Lotto advertising business, valued at $6 million.

ROME - Italian phone lovers, facing some of the highest call charges in Europe, can now use the telephone for free, provided they don't mind commercials cutting into their conversation, reports Corriere della Sera newspaper. Promotion System Phone is carrying out a trial in which calls are interrupted by a 10-second ad after the first minute and then once every three minutes.

MINNEAPOLIS - General Mills Inc. will break the first in a series of three new 15-second TV commercials for its newly acquired Chex Mix snack brand next week, it says. The commercials, the first work for Chex Mix from Campbell Mithun Esty, Minneapolis, are part of a $25 million ad campaign designed to reposition Chex Mix as an all-family brand.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

LONDON - Orange Plc, Britain's third biggest mobile telephone company, is considering the launch of new services such as Internet browsing, home shopping, on-line newspapers and financial services and narrow-band television, it says. Orange will double to 800 million pounds its investments in its network, to fund these new services which it hopes will win new customers.

NEW YORK - Armed with its just-acquired LIN Television Corp stations, the private investment firm Hicks, Muse, Tate & Furst Inc will move aggressively into broadcasting, either acquiring more big-city stations or adding mid-market outlets, analysts say.

NEW YORK - CBS Inc says it has signed an affiliation deal with Tele-Communications Inc that would allow CBS Eye on People, its cable television network, the first step in being carried on the cable systems of TCI, the largest cable operator in the United States.

MADRID - Spain's Telefonica has agreed to sell part of its stake in CanalSatelite, a digital television platform owned by France's Canal Plus that competes with its own Via Digital, the national stock market commission says.

LONDON - A British Methodist preacher is taking to the Internet to offer mourners a chance to pay electronic respects at virtual graves. David Wilkinson is charging 150 pounds to set up an epitaph on the global computer network which includes a 1,000-word obituary, photo and copy of the death certificate.

FRANKFURT - Private TV station Wetter Kanal (Weather Channel) says it plans to offer local forecasts for 100 cities and regions by the end of the year, in an attempt to boost ratings. A study by market research firms IRES and Emnid showed that 1.9 million viewers watch the channel at least once a day.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LONDON - Emerging markets in Latin America and Asia are fuelling growth in the $40 billion global music business, says a report by the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry. Unit sales rose 20 percent in Latin America last year, the fastest growth rate in the world.

NEW YORK - The American Medical Association has agreed to allow its name to be used in endorsing a line of products made by Sunbeam Corp, the New York Times reports. Under the agreement, royalty payments potentially totaling millions from Sunbeam will go to the AMA, to be used for health, education and research programs.

AUBURN HILLS, Michigan - Chrysler Corp. announces its average 1998 model year price will be down 0.6 percent, making it the only member of the U.S. Big Three automakers, the others being Ford and General Motors Corp, to slash prices amid an industry-wide price war.

MONTREAL - Seagram Co Ltd's Spirits and Wines group says growth in key brands such as Captain Morgan Rum and "excellent" sales of its Tropicana Beverage Group's Pure Premium juice in North America boosted net income for the fourth quarter ended June 30 to $148 million from $89 million last year.

MEXICO CITY - Heavy demand for Thursday's initial public stock offering by Mexico's TV Azteca is another sign that the country's equity market is back on the map after two years in the doldrums, analysts say. *********

LONDON - The British Tourist Authority sparks a bout of nationalist fury by deciding to drop the distinctive Union Jack flag as its logo. The authority, which promotes the 40 billion pound industry worldwide, is opting for a new logo because the Union Jack has a "triumphal, colonial feel", it says.

LONDON - Sales of new "R" registration cars in Britain have soared in the first month of availability, newspapers report. Figures from the industry's Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders show 208,000 registrations were recorded in the first 10 days of August, which could mean the whole month would see record-breaking sales of well over 500,000, says the Independent.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

TOKYO - Japanese drivers can now get a hot oil treatment for their car and their hair simultaneously as the Japan Energy Corp introduces the "Hair Station" -- auto service coupled with a second-floor beauty salon, making a bouffant and a battery charge a one-stop shop.

BANGKOK - Thailand hopes to use its weak currency to win back foreign tourists in a two-year "Amazing Thailand" promotion which it believes will earn the country one trillion baht ($32 billion). The Tourism Authority of Thailand, expects more than 17 million foreign tourists in 1998 and 1999, earning the country 600 billion baht in much-needed foreign currency, said a senior tourism official.
